Sun.name: Moroccan Spiced Chicken Thighs with Cornmeal Flatbread

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Pat chicken thighs dry and rub all over with Moroccan spice and 1 tbsp olive oil. Season with salt.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high. Sear chicken skin-side down 5 minutes until golden, flip and sear 2 more minutes.
Add garlic, canned tomatoes, and golden raisins to the skillet. Nestle chicken into sauce and transfer skillet to oven. Roast 35–40 minutes until chicken is cooked through (165°F).
While chicken roasts, bring 3 cups salted water to boil. Whisk in cornmeal in a slow stream, reduce heat to low.
Stir cornmeal constantly 5–7 minutes until thick and pulling from sides. Stir in butter. Season with salt.
Spread cornmeal onto a parchment-lined baking sheet to about 1/2-inch thick. Let rest 5 minutes, then slice into wedges.
Serve chicken and sauce over or alongside cornmeal flatbread wedges. Spoon extra pan sauce over everything.
recipe.notes: Kid tip: Serve the mild, sweet tomato-raisin sauce separately as a dipping sauce. Cornmeal wedges are finger-food friendly.

Mon.name: Soba Noodle Bowl with Mushrooms & Soft-Boiled Egg

steps: Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Gently lower eggs in and cook 7 minutes, then transfer to an ice bath. Peel and halve when cooled.
Cook soba noodles according to package directions (usually 4–5 min). Drain and rinse under cold water to prevent sticking; set aside.
In a medium saucepan, warm the soba/udon broth over medium heat. Add soy sauce, ginger, and garlic; simmer 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat neutral oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sauté mushrooms 5–6 minutes until golden and slightly crispy. Season lightly with salt.
Divide noodles among three bowls. Ladle hot broth over noodles. Top with sautéed mushrooms, a halved soft-boiled egg, a drizzle of sesame oil, and green onions.
For the picky eater, serve broth on the side for dipping if preferred.
recipe.notes: Keep toppings modular so the 8-year-old can customize their bowl. Candy cap mushrooms can be rehydrated and added alongside regular mushrooms for deeper flavor.

side.name: Steamed Broccoli with Sesame Drizzle
steps: Steam broccoli florets over boiling water for 4–5 minutes until bright green and just tender.
Whisk together sesame oil and soy sauce; drizzle over broccoli.
Sprinkle with chia seeds if desired and serve immediately alongside the noodle bowls.

Tue.name: Ground Beef Tacos with Dried Chili Sauce

steps: Toast dried chilis in a dry skillet 30 seconds per side until fragrant. Place in a bowl, cover with boiling water, and soak 10 minutes.
Drain chilis and blend with canned tomatoes, garlic, and 1/4 cup soaking liquid until smooth. Season with salt.
Brown ground beef in the skillet over medium-high, breaking up with a spoon, about 5–6 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Pour chili sauce over beef. Simmer 5 minutes until sauce thickens and coats meat. Adjust salt.
Warm tortillas directly on a gas burner 30 seconds per side, or in a dry skillet.
Set up a taco bar with cheese, sour cream, and lime wedges. Let the family build their own tacos.
Kid option: Serve beef without chili sauce on a separate plain tortilla with just cheese if needed.
recipe.notes: Ancho chilis are mild and slightly sweet — great gateway for kids. Guajillo adds more heat; use ancho for kid-friendliest result.

Wed.name: Red Lentil Soup with Crusty Bread

steps: Heat olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add onion and cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add garlic and Moroccan spice. Cook 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant.
Add rinsed red lentils, canned tomatoes, and chicken stock. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer uncovered 20–25 minutes until lentils are completely soft and beginning to fall apart.
Use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup — leave some texture. Or blend half and stir back in.
Add lemon juice and season generously with salt and pepper. Add a splash of water if too thick.
Ladle into bowls and serve with crusty bread or toast for dipping.
recipe.notes: This soup freezes beautifully — make a double batch if time allows. Kid-friendly when blended smooth; serve bread for dipping fun.

steps: Reheat Wednesday's red lentil soup on the stovetop over medium heat, adding a splash of water or broth to loosen if needed.
Alternatively, reheat Sunday's Moroccan chicken thighs in a 350°F oven for 15 minutes, covered with foil.
Warm leftover taco meat in a skillet with a splash of water to refresh the sauce.
recipe.notes: Remix idea: Stuff leftover taco meat into a quesadilla with remaining cheese for a quick Thursday lunch or dinner upgrade.

recipe.notes: Remix idea: Spoon leftover red lentil soup into a bowl, top with a soft-fried egg and a drizzle of olive oil for a protein-boosted Friday dinner.
